text.tspan: Ship a small working version first,
then improve it with real feedback
An internship or junior role in web
development, where I can learn from
I build web apps that are quick to use and easy to keep running.
I'm a fourth-year IT student who builds web apps and cares about making them easy to use. I'm still
learning, but I like finishing things people can actually click through.
It started with a broken layout.
I started coding in my first year of college. A simple HTML page for a class activity took me a whole
weekend because I kept breaking the layout. It was frustrating, but when it finally worked I wanted to
build more. From there I moved to JavaScript, then databases, then full-stack apps.
Two days on the wrong thing.
The hardest bug I've had was in our capstone: data saved fine but never showed up on the next page. I
spent two days checking the screen before I found the problem was in my database query. Now I read the
error and check the data first, before touching the UI.
Outside of code I play games, mostly with friends, and I always have music on while I work. Games taught
me to be okay with losing a few times before getting something right, which helps a lot when debugging.
A team and real code reviews.
I want an internship or junior web developer role where I can work with a team, get code reviews, and get
better at backend work and clean project structure.
